answer_summary: E = n(CH4)/day x |dH2000| = [101325 Pa x 2.2e5 m3 s-1 x 86400 s / (8.31 J mol-1 K-1 x 298 K)] x 781876 J mol-1 = 6.080980774...e17 J day-1, i.e. 6.08e17 J day-1 to three significant figures (raw exact rational 25098031949760000000000/41273 J day-1). The 4.6/4.7 enthalpies were derived inline: dH298 = -802.3 kJ/mol (Hess), dH2000 = -781.876 kJ/mol (Kirchhoff, dCp = 12 J mol-1 K-1), so no printed fallback was used.
assumptions: Q in 'volumetric flow Q = 2.2 x 10^5 m3' is interpreted as a volumetric flow RATE of 2.2e5 m3 s-1 (the daily gas volume is Q x 86400 s); the official PDF clips the time basis of the unit at a line break, and the physical/fallback context only supports the flow-rate reading. All Lean definitions keep Q symbolic, so the derivation is exact for any restored unit.
Gas constant R = 8.31 J mol-1 K-1 taken as an ordinary scientific reference value (trusted_general_law); no value of R is printed in the paper. Result is insensitive at 3 s.f. to using 8.314.

Kirchhoff correction uses the Cp part only (dH2000 = dH298 + dCp*dT), matching the per-mole-of-CH4, all-gaseous, constant-Cp convention of parts 4.6-4.7 and the printed data; fallbacks (-750, -700 kJ/mol) not used.
Three-significant-figure reporting with half-away-from-zero ties via IChO2026Chem.Reporting.ReportsAtQuantum; quantum 1e15 J day-1.
source_gaps: Unit of the volumetric flow Q is printed as 'm3' with the time unit clipped at a line break in theory_problem.pdf (PDF page 39, confirmed at word level); the flow-rate reading Q = 2.2e5 m3 s-1 is the physically and contextually forced interpretation but is formally a source gap (flagged, not silently assumed).
No gas constant is printed anywhere in the problem materials; R supplied from general scientific reference.
If instead Q were read as a daily volume, E would be 7.04e12 J day-1; if a PV-converted enthalpy convention were used, E = 6.19e17 J day-1. Both alternatives are documented in answer.md.
